correctness.rationale: Every leaf copies its core's previous bit, making all blocks coherent in one update, even when some first-round core bits are random. Strict leaf dominance then gives the deterministic swap of core and leaf words. Its diagonal gives 2^k fixed states, while the other 4^k−2^k words pair off; no noncoherent state can recur. Conditional on the initial core word, the independent leaf blocks and tie coins give the product law for the new core word, with the two orientations summed only for distinct words. A block contributes (t_v+1)(a_v+b_v)/2 to the long-run average, and unconditional neighbor colors are independent Bernoulli-p at time zero. Adding one vote with fair ties gives M_2r=M_(2r−1); adding two odd-to-odd gains from counts r−1 and loses from counts r, with net sign 2p−1 in the interior. Positive core degrees give s_v≥3 and hence strictness. On P_k the degree sum is 2k−2, giving 4k−2 vertices and maximum degree 5.
residual_risks: Only the proof certifies arbitrary finite eligible cores and all real p. Strict amplification is in expected long-run occupancy, not pathwise amplification or consensus.

value.rationale: The invariant coherence reduces a stochastic process with potentially many attractors to an exactly solvable one-step class distribution. Distinguishing expected bias amplification from consensus matters on these graphs, since many of their recurrent classes blink. A bounded-degree tree family shows that exponentially many recurrent classes can coexist with one-step absorption.
residual_risks: The formula does not describe arbitrary graphs without strict private-leaf dominance or a different update rule.
